content:
In our previous studies we have been following the beautiful progression of the silver trumpets that Yahweh commanded Moses to make in the wilderness.

We first heard the long blast of both trumpets together, which gathered the entire congregation before the Tabernacle. We then heard the sound of a single trumpet, which called only the leaders of Israel to come and receive instruction from Moses. After that came the sharp alarm that caused the camp to break its rest and begin its journey through the wilderness toward the Promised Land. Each sound had its own clear meaning, and each one moved the nation forward in the purpose of Yahweh. Today we come to the fourth sound of the silver trumpets, and this one carries a very different message from all the others.

Yahweh declared to Israel: "And if ye go to war in your land against the enemy that oppresseth you, then ye shall blow an alarm with the trumpets; and ye shall be remembered before Yahweh your God, and ye shall be saved from your enemies" (Numbers 10:9). This was not the sound of gathering. It was not the sound of journeying. It was the sound of battle. Let us imagine the scene for a moment. Israel has now left its place of rest. The camp is moving through the wilderness exactly as Yahweh has commanded. The cloud leads them by day and the pillar of fire by night. Tribe after tribe marches in perfect order, each in its appointed place. And yet, sooner or later, an enemy appears on the horizon. The peaceful march suddenly becomes a battlefield.

At that moment, the priests lift the silver trumpets once again. A sharp alarm echoes across the whole camp, and every soldier immediately recognises its meaning. The battle has begun. The alarm gathers the army, it strengthens their courage, and it reminds every Israelite that they do not fight alone. But more importantly, Yahweh attaches a wonderful promise to this trumpet blast.

He says that when they sound the alarm, they will be remembered before Him, and that He Himself will save them from their enemies. We must understand this promise rightly. It does not mean that Yahweh had forgotten His people and then suddenly remembered them because of the trumpet. Rather, the trumpet was the visible sign of Israel placing all their confidence in Yahweh's covenant. As they cried out to Him, He acted faithfully on their behalf.

Victory would never come because Israel possessed stronger weapons or larger armies. Victory belonged to Yahweh alone.

This fourth trumpet completes a beautiful progression that we have been studying throughout Numbers chapter ten. First, the two trumpets gathered the entire congregation. Next, one trumpet gathered the leaders for instruction. Then the alarm sounded for the camp to begin its journey. And the alarm sounds again; not to move the camp this time, but to prepare the people for war. And when we look closely, we see that this is exactly how our life unfolds. First, God gathers us to Himself through the Gospel. Then He teaches and prepares us through His Word. Next, He calls us to walk the narrow way through the wilderness of this world. And finally, we discover that our journey is also a battlefield.

Many believers imagine that once they come to Christ, life will somehow become free from conflict and struggle. But the Scriptures teach us the very opposite. The moment we begin following Christ, we enter a spiritual war unlike any earthly battle we have ever known. And we must understand clearly who our enemies are. They are not flesh and blood. We are not fighting against other people, against nations, or against governments. The apostle Paul explains the true nature of our warfare when he writes: "For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places" (Ephesians 6:12). Our battle is against sin, against the desires of our fallen flesh, against false doctrine, against temptation, and against the whole spirit of this present world that constantly seeks to draw us away from God.

Every disciple of Christ is enlisted into this battle. This is why Paul repeatedly describes believers as soldiers. Writing to Timothy, he says: "Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier" (2 Timothy 2:3-4). Notice the language Paul uses. Christ has chosen us to be soldiers. Every believer has been enlisted into His army. Our lives are no longer our own; we now live to please our Commander. Paul uses this same language when speaking about his fellow workers. He calls Epaphroditus his "brother, and companion in labour, and fellow soldier" (Philippians 2:25). He refers to Archippus as "our fellow soldier" (Philemon 2). The early congregation did not see itself merely as a gathering of worshippers. It understood that it was an army marching under the authority of Christ.

Just as Israel followed Joshua into battle, so we follow the greater Joshua; the Messiah. The writer to the Hebrews describes Him as "the captain of their salvation" (Hebrews 2:10). He is the One who goes before His people. He never asks His soldiers to fight a battle that He Himself has not already won.
And unlike the armies of Israel, our weapons are not physical. We do not carry swords or spears of iron. Paul reminds us: "For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds" (2 Corinthians 10:4). The battlefield is spiritual, and therefore our weapons must be spiritual too. Because of this, Yahweh has not left His soldiers unprepared or unprotected. Paul urges every believer: "Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil" (Ephesians 6:11).

He then describes the armour that every soldier of Christ must wear. Around our waist is the belt of truth. Protecting our hearts is the breastplate of righteousness. Our feet are prepared with the Gospel of peace. In one hand we hold the shield of faith, with which we are able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked one. Upon our head rests the helmet of salvation. And in our hand we carry the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God. Notice carefully something very important here; the only offensive weapon in all this armour is the Word of God. Everything else protects and defends us, but the sword that strikes the enemy is the living Word of God. And this brings us back once again to the silver trumpets.

In the days of Moses, the trumpet rallied the army for battle. Today, it is the living Word of Yahweh that performs the very same work. Every time the Scriptures are faithfully preached, the trumpet sounds again. It awakens sleeping soldiers. It strengthens weary hearts. It exposes the enemy and his schemes. It reminds us of our Commander. And it calls the army of Christ to stand together in unity and courage. The trumpet of truth is still sounding throughout the whole earth. And as we hear that sound, we remember that victory has never depended upon human strength. David understood this when he stood before Goliath, a giant far greater than himself, and declared: "The battle is Yahweh's" (1 Samuel 17:47). Paul echoes the very same confidence when he asks: "If God be for us, who can be against us?" (Romans 8:31).

The promise attached to the battle trumpet in Numbers is just as encouraging for us today as it was for Israel in the wilderness. Yahweh promised Israel that He would save them from their enemies. And the New Testament reveals the glorious fulfilment of that promise when Paul triumphantly declares: "Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him that loved us" (Romans 8:37). Notice carefully that Paul does not say we avoid the battles altogether. He says that in the midst of every battle we are more than conquerors, because Christ fights together with us. Every single day the alarm trumpet continues to sound in the lives of God's people. It calls us to resist temptation with holiness, to answer fear with faith, to overcome discouragement with hope, to defend the truth against false teaching, to respond to hatred with love, and to crucify the desires of the flesh through the power of the Spirit.

The New creation life is not a life of comfort and ease. It is a life of faithful warfare. Yet we do not march into battle alone. Our Captain walks before us. Our armour has already been provided for us. Our weapons are mighty through God. The Spirit strengthens us continually, and the promises of Yahweh assure us that He will never leave us nor forsake us. Just as the priests once sounded the silver trumpets and Yahweh delivered Israel from their enemies, so today the trumpet of His Word continues to strengthen us, the New Creation. As faithful soldiers of Christ, we stand together, clothed in the whole armour of God, fighting the good fight of faith, until the day when our Captain defeats every enemy; sin, the adversary, and even death itself, is finally and forever destroyed. On that day the warfare will be finished, and the army of the Lamb will enter the everlasting Kingdom in complete and unbroken victory.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God and our Deliverer,

We thank You that we never march into battle alone.

You have given us a Captain who goes before us,

armour that covers us, and a Word that is mighty to pull down every stronghold.

When the alarm sounds and the enemy appears, teach us not to trust our own strength,

but to remember that the battle is Yours, and the victory belongs to You.

Make us faithful soldiers; resisting temptation, defending the truth,

answering fear with faith and hatred with love, until our Captain returns.

"Yahweh is a man of war; Yahweh is His name"; and greatly to be praised.

In the name of our Captain and Messiah we pray. Amen.
